key_insight: Greedy decoding in LLMs is not fully deterministic: the same prompt and model can produce different outputs in BF16 versus FP16 because tiny precision changes can flip the top token and cascade through generation.
engineering_relevance: Inference systems that assume precision-invariant greedy decoding may see reproducibility failures; selective FP32 recomputation of the LM head can improve agreement with low latency cost in small-batch settings.
method: Compared BF16 vs FP16 greedy decoding on identical hardware across 6 models, 3 benchmarks, and up to 12B parameters
Analyzed error propagation to relate output flips to top-2 logit margin versus directional perturbation at the LM head
Tested a selective FP32 LM-head recomputation trigger when the margin falls below a threshold
evidence_signal: Across the evaluated models and benchmarks, 49-100% of prompts diverged across precisions, and the best mitigation improved exact agreement by +22-36 percentage points on A10G with under 4% latency overhead at batch size ≤4.
watch_item: The mitigation is not universal: its benefit declines when body-layer error dominates, especially at batch size ≥8 and under end-to-end FP8.
paper_title: Greedy Decoding Is Not Precision-Invariant: Cross-Precision Output Divergence in LLM Inference
